chapters.title: 01 · Scale and floor
chapters.text: All coordinates are in metres. The four-person cabin floor is 1.58 m above ground; a 1.80 m human figure provides a reference for checking the usable space.

chapters.title: 02 · Cabin frame and clearances
chapters.text: The interior is 3.56 m wide. A clear aisle of at least 72 cm remains between the seats, with more than 2 m of headroom beside the sloping roof shoulders.

chapters.title: 03 · Four energy-absorbing seats
chapters.text: Two pilots sit in front and two passengers behind, all facing forward. The seat cushions are approximately 55 cm above the cabin floor; each seat has a separate headrest and safety harness.

chapters.title: 04 · Cockpit and controls
chapters.text: Build two sloping instrument consoles, separate control sticks and pedals. The consoles sit ahead of the seats while the central aisle remains clear.

chapters.title: 05 · Life support and storage
chapters.text: Equipment lockers, an air-treatment unit and reserve cylinders occupy the aft wall. Luggage stays clear of the crew entrance and central aisle.

chapters.title: 06 · Side walls and window openings
chapters.text: Separate wall bands and posts surround the windows. The glazing has alpha 0.1 with actual openings behind it. A 1.10 × 2.00 m crew entrance remains on the aft starboard side.

chapters.title: 07 · Faceted nose and cockpit
chapters.text: The nose narrows toward the front. Two sloping planes form the windshield, with triangular side glazing facets; every glass panel is a separate planar solid.

chapters.title: 08 · Roof and cabin lighting
chapters.text: The roof is a separate panel group. Interior / cutaway hides this group and the port-side wall, keeping the completed cabin accessible for inspection.

chapters.title: 09 · Exterior armor and service panels
chapters.text: Ceramic-colored hull panels receive a dark impact protection belt and orange identification stripes. The aft service covers align with the interior life-support equipment.

chapters.title: 10 · Engines and auxiliary systems
chapters.text: Two open-bell main engines are fitted below the floor. The side pods stop ahead of the crew entrance, keeping the door and ramp approach clear.

chapters.title: 11 · Four stable landing legs
chapters.text: The bottom of each landing pad lies exactly on the y = 0 ground plane. Outward-splayed legs provide a footprint almost 7 m wide, with individual joints, shock absorbers and diagonal braces.

chapters.title: 12 · Opening door and crew ramp
chapters.text: Rotate the actual door around its hinge. The 1.10 m wide ramp has anti-slip cross treads and two handrails, with its lower landing resting on the ground.

chapters.title: 13 · Attitude control, sensors and lights
chapters.text: Four corner blocks receive lateral and vertical attitude-control nozzles. Add two landing lights and a terrain sensor on the nose, plus a short communications antenna above.

chapters.title: 14 · Finishing the exterior
chapters.text: Fit the thermal panels, identification markings and entrance light. Cabin items remain separate objects; the roof and port-side wall can be hidden in the cutaway view.

chapters.title: 15 · Aft hull and connecting passage
chapters.text: Open the original cabin through its aft wall. The crew module and hangar continue at the same 1.58 m deck level, preserving the original seats and cockpit dimensions.

chapters.title: 16 · Rooms and pressure-tight passage
chapters.text: The central corridor serves a washroom, galley and four-berth crew room. A pressure bulkhead and a sliding door separate the hangar from the crew spaces.

chapters.title: 17 · Washroom, shower and galley
chapters.text: The port-side module contains a washbasin, shower tray and toilet, followed by a galley with storage. Fixtures follow the 1.58 m deck level and retain human-scale dimensions.

chapters.title: 18 · Four-berth crew quarters
chapters.text: Build two separate bunk-bed units for four people. Each berth is 2.10 m long, with about 1 m between levels, plus a pillow, restraint strap, reading light and ladder.

chapters.title: 19 · Overhead crane and cargo handling
chapters.text: The recorded construction sequence lifts the crate, moves it sideways and aft, then lowers it onto the securing area. The hook and cable retract afterward, leaving the central cargo lane clear.

chapters.title: 20 · Large main engine pods
chapters.text: Build two long side-mounted engine pods, approximately 2.1 m in diameter, with open aft nozzles. They leave the central hangar door and cargo ramp approach unobstructed.

chapters.title: 21 · Four lift engines and aft landing supports
chapters.text: Replace the original small engine pair with four larger vertical nozzles. Two additional aft landing legs support the extended cargo hull on the ground.

chapters.title: 22 · Opening cargo doors and wide ramp
chapters.text: Two separate cargo door leaves rotate around their hinges. The opening provides approximately 4.6 m clear width and connects to a 4.5 m wide, gently sloping ramp that rests on the ground.

chapters.title: 23 · Crew module and hangar exterior
chapters.text: Separate hull panels enclose the extension. The roofs and port-side panels can be removed in cutaway view; the observation windows retain alpha 0.1.

chapters.title: 24 · Wings, ailerons and flaps
chapters.text: The swept main wing spans approximately 14.8 m, with a thicker root, thinner tip and slight dihedral. Inboard flaps and outboard ailerons are separate bodies with their own hinge shafts.

chapters.title: 25 · Twin tail fins and elevators
chapters.text: Fit two outward-canted vertical stabilizers with separate rudders. Horizontal stabilizers attach above the hangar door, keeping the rear loading route open.

chapters.title: 26 · Cargo variant final inspection
chapters.text: Complete LARK-4C with room signs, a crane control console and aft maneuvering thrusters. Inspect the hangar and crew quarters in dedicated views; the extension remains part of the original construction tutorial.
